Pele Yoetz 75:2: And the Torah scholar shall not listen to the voice of whisperers who say that such is the way of the great Torah scholars of Israel, who go out to the marketplace from time to time - such as on Friday, or Saturday night, or some summer day - to stroll. These men are agents of the evil inclination and second-rate converts. You too say to them: leave the great men of Israel be, for they knew what they were doing and their intention was pleasing to Heaven, and we know nothing but what the Torah said (Joshua 1:8), "this book of the Torah shall not depart from your mouth," and it is written (Job 7:19), "You do not let me alone even long enough to swallow my saliva" - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said that even for the time it takes to swallow saliva, a person is called to account for the World to Come. Woe to us on the day of judgment and the day of rebuke. And there is no better stroll than the study house, which is a paradise for the righteous and causes them to stroll in the Garden of Eden. And let him reason a fortiori from a person occupied with his workers or his accounts, who does not concern himself with people's honor and does not go among people or stroll - all the more so we, whose day is short and whose work is much, longer than the measure of the earth - even if a man lived a thousand years, it would not suffice him, and time is precious and every moment he loses is a great, irretrievable loss. And the sages of ethics have already written that this is like one to whom it is said, "take for yourself a great treasury of gold coins and count them, and whatever you count shall be yours" - he would not slumber nor sleep, would not grow tired nor weary, counting on with all his strength. All the more so for earning the life of the World to Come and giving peace of mind to his Maker - of this it is said (Proverbs 2:4): "if you seek it as silver and search for it as for hidden treasures, then you shall understand the fear of the LORD."
Pele Yoetz 75:3: However, there is walking that is a mitzvah, in the manner of what is written (Exodus 18:20), "and you shall show them the way they shall walk in it" - this refers to accompanying the dead, escorting a bride, visiting the sick, and comforting mourners and the like (Bava Metzia 30b). But one must weigh in the balance and stand guard so that a mitzvah not come through a transgression and so that its reward not be lost through its loss, God forbid. And it is known that for a mitzvah that can be performed by others, Torah study is preferable, as it is written (Proverbs 8:11), "and all desirable things cannot compare to it." However, sometimes the neglect of Torah is itself its fulfillment (see Menachot 99b), and it is fitting for a Torah scholar to run to a mitzvah and be counted among his colleagues for a mitzvah matter, so that others see and do likewise, and the merit of the many depends on him.
Pele Yoetz 76:1: Exactingness - Exactingness is the offspring of pride, consuming from soul to flesh, for such a person's life is not truly life, and offspring follow from fathers and offspring of offspring - it causes hatred, rivalry, division, and slander, and many such evils. And whoever is exacting is dealt with exactingly from Heaven for every transgression, matter (Yoma 23a) - correspondingly, whoever overlooks his own attributes, they overlook all his transgressions, and even his own flesh shall dwell securely. And it is true that the trait of exactingness is a spirit within man, an evil trait from the womb and from conception, and whoever's nature is not to be exacting at all - this is a gift of God; and so, in this manner, with all evil and forbidden traits. But man has dominion over his own spirit, and through his own daily efforts with pure thoughts and diligence in books of ethics, he has the power to exchange his traits, evil for good, and to turn away from the snares of death and keep the way of life. And a few matters a person should take to heart to be saved from the trait of exactingness - they are written above under the entry "Ahavat Re'im" [love of fellows] and under the entry "Ga'avah" [pride] - let the wise man hear and increase learning.
Pele Yoetz 76:2: And it is especially necessary to be diligent not to be exacting with his wife, his servants, and the members of his household, for the inclination nearby doubly incites him to become filled with rage and be very exacting when they act against his own will. But the man who fears the LORD, then, shall humble his heart and reason: behold, I am born of woman like him, and if I am honored and served because of my own fortune, that the LORD has graced me with wealth and honor, it is possible that before Heaven he is more honored than I - as they said on the verse (Job 3:19), "the small and the great are there." A stranger and a freed slave are sometimes greater than their masters. And if he is obligated in my honor because he receives a small benefit through me, or because the Creator commanded him regarding my honor, all the more so am I obligated in the honor of my Creator, my Former, and my Maker, who has favored His good upon me and bestowed good kindnesses upon me beyond fathoming and beyond number, while I provoke Him - and even so, I fall short in His service and provoke Him to His face. Woe is me, for according to my own deeds my recompense shall be repaid, and it is known that with the measure a person measures, they measure to him (Megillah 12b). Of such and similar matters, the living person shall take to heart and strengthen himself day by day, and he shall repent and be healed.
Pele Yoetz 76:3: However, it is fitting to hold fast to the trait of exactingness regarding his fellow - to be exacting about his fellow's honor and not to act against his fellow's own will, and not to do anything against his will even the slightest bit - for whoever pains his fellow is as though he pained the whole world, and God shall bring everything into judgment, even if he only killed a louse in his fellow's presence, causing him disgust and distress (Chagigah 5a), even without intending to cause him distress. And whoever goes deep into this shall have his flesh shudder, and shall stand guard over whatever comes to his hand, and shall seek mercy from the One who graces man with knowledge, that He set him right with good counsel to do the good and the upright in the eyes of God and man - for sometimes what a person thinks will find favor in his fellow's eyes actually pains him. And every clever person shall act with knowledge, and flee very much from anything where there is even a one-in-a-thousand concern that the spirit of his fellow creatures might not be at ease with him, and shall treat every person as suspect as a robber yet honor him as [he would] Rabban Gamliel, and the LORD shall not withhold good from those who walk in innocence, and Heaven shall assist him that the spirit of his fellow creatures be at ease with him and he find favor and good sense in the eyes of God and man. And all the more so must one be exacting and concerned for his Maker's honor, to do all that is in his power - mitzvot, good deeds, and matters of piety - to give peace of mind to his Maker, and to flee from transgression and from transgressing the fine details of mitzvot and the fine details of the Sages, even the smallest of details, for His honor is great and our obligation is great beyond fathoming, to serve with all our soul and all our heart to give peace of mind to our Former, and not to cause any distress, anger, or blemish above, heaven forbid. Happy is the man who fears the LORD - let him awaken from his slumber and not be asleep, for this applies to every person.
Pele Yoetz 77:1: Seclusion - Seclusion is a proper preparation for faithful reading, to dwell in the depth of halachah - it shall add power to understand a matter thoroughly and to render a true judgment in its truth. It is also the cornerstone for arranging holiness, thinking pure thoughts, reckoning with one's Maker the world's own accounting, and arousing the sparks of love and fear - and one's hand attains this when nothing disturbs. And likewise, to pour out conversation to seek forgiveness before the LORD requires rest. Therefore it is good for a man to designate for himself a dwelling place that is his alone, with no strangers present, to seclude himself there to study and acquire an order of holiness - and if he has only one house with the members of his household, let him rise while it is still night, when all are asleep, and seclude himself with his Maker, for in one hour of seclusion he can study and understand and acquire an order of holiness more than in a whole day. And seclusion is a great fence to guard his mouth, a restraint from sin with his tongue, and I have already noted a sign: "he shall wear the holy linen." And those who make their ways straight, even while standing in the assembly of the people and in the streets of the city, seclude themselves in their own minds with their Maker, and let their company not disturb them, in the manner of the Psalmist's saying: "when I stand among Your congregation, O Rock, to exalt You, I bend and bow my head and stature" - meaning, let their company not disturb me, as written in Sefer Chasidim (17). Happy is he who attains this trait - how good is his portion and how pleasant is his lot, always occupied with the mitzvah of fearing and loving the honored and awesome LORD and cleaving to Him - this is a great principle in the Torah and in the virtue of the righteous, who always walk before God, and this is the root that bears the fruit of the righteous - it is a tree of life to those who hold fast to it. And a fence for this is to keep one's eyes lowered, and thereby he shall remember to lift his heart along with his hands to God in heaven. The righteous shall be tested and see that the matter is proper for fear and love, and one mitzvah draws another.
Pele Yoetz 78:1: Preparation - Preparation for the Sabbath is a great mitzvah. We find great men of Israel who occupied themselves with it. And it has already been written in the name of the Ari, of blessed memory, that whoever sweats to prepare the needs of the Sabbath performs a great repair for the blemish of the covenant. And it was said of our master, Rabbi Avraham HaLevi, of blessed memory, that he would take many steps to buy and prepare the needs of the Sabbath one by one, for there is reward for steps, and he would do everything himself, since a mitzvah performed personally is greater than one performed through an agent (Kiddushin 41a). And I say that the master did so because even in his walking, his Torah was his occupation in his thought, or he was occupied in cleaving to his Maker and His love and fear, as stated just above - but we, orphans of orphans, if we have someone to do our work, it is better that we sit at home and occupy ourselves with the holy Torah and acquire new knowledge, for "all desirable things cannot compare to it," even the desirable things of Heaven, as is known. In any case, he should not fail to buy something or prepare something, such as arranging the table and trimming the lamps and lengthening the wicks and the like, to fulfill the mitzvah of preparation. And the disciples of the Ari, of blessed memory, have already written that according to the mystical secret of these matters, the trimming of the lamps should be done by a man.
Pele Yoetz 78:2: And likewise every preparation a person makes for a mitzvah matter is itself considered a mitzvah. Behold, therefore, whoever's every deed is for the sake of Heaven is found to be occupied with mitzvot all his days. And how good it is to express with one's lips, before every deed, that he is making preparation for a mitzvah - for example, before eating, let him say: I hereby come to eat and drink so that my body be healthy and strong for the service of God, blessed be He. And before sleep, let him say: I hereby lie down to sleep so that my mind be clear and settled for the service of God, blessed be He. And before going out to do business, let him say: I hereby go to conduct business and strive to earn, with the help of Heaven, in order to support the members of my household as my Creator commanded me, and so that I may perform charity and acts of kindness and all the mitzvot properly. And likewise when building a house or making a garment and the like, and so on in this manner with every deed he does. And his words bear fruit, for spirituality and holiness rest upon physical matters, and it shall be counted a mitzvah for him, and moreover he receives reward even for these words - provided his deeds match his words, that he not eat and drink too much to distend his stomach, but rather "the righteous eats to satisfy his soul," and not sleep too much, and not be obsessed and labor too much to grow rich, for there is no restraint upon the LORD to save and enrich, whether by much or by little - and since he does everything for the need of his Maker's service, he should not neglect his service because of his eating, sleeping, and business, for then deed comes and contradicts speech, and the One who dwells in heaven laughs at him. And likewise, since he does everything in the name of a mitzvah, he must be all the more diligent that a mitzvah not come through a transgression. And he shall be careful with his eating and drinking and business that they be according to law and precept, and then it shall be counted a mitzvah both beforehand and afterward, and reward is established for him. So shall he be careful with his eating to follow what is beneficial and not what is pleasant to his palate and harmful, for besides that it would not be pleasing and would not be counted a mitzvah, he shall also be punished for transgressing what the Torah said (Deuteronomy 4:15): "and you shall greatly guard your souls."
Pele Yoetz 78:3: And there is another kind of preparation that is in his own body, in the manner of what is written (Amos 4:12): "prepare to meet your God, O Israel" - namely, such as washing his face before the morning prayer, and if he stands barefoot he must also wash his feet and make sure they are not soiled, and likewise he shall prepare to meet his God in his clothing - even when he prays at night alone in his house, he should not stand to pray except in the manner and custom of the place for standing before dignitaries. And it is likewise when he occupies himself with Torah, since the Shechinah is opposite him - his clothing shall be proper, and he shall sit in a dignified manner, as one sitting before the king. And also when he reclines at his table, and especially when he recites Grace after Meals to the King of glory, he must sit in a dignified manner, for this is the table that is before the LORD. And there is a known, awesome incident that happened to our master, Rabbi Yisrael Nagara, in the time of the Ari, of blessed memory. How good it would be to be careful to wrap oneself in the outer garment called "beinish" (in German: "Uberkleid") during prayer time (and we have heard with our own ears about the master "Beit David," whose custom, a holy custom, was to wrap himself in a "beinish" when he sat to judge, for the honor of the Shechinah, which judges among the judges - may his merit shield us).
Pele Yoetz 78:4: And there is another, great kind of preparation - namely, preparation of the mind, that he not do anything, small or great, suddenly, but rather, before doing any deed, take it to heart and consider in his mind whether it is fitting to do it, or whether it is better to sit and not do it. And it is especially necessary to be careful and diligent regarding speech, for the tongue is quick to speak, and much speech is harsh, evil to Heaven and evil to people, while little of it is good - all of a man's labor is for his mouth, as is known, that the evil of speech is great. Therefore, before he says anything, let him clarify his own conversation in his mind and weigh it in the balance and scale of judgment - whether he is forced to speak for the sake of a mitzvah or for his own need, let him speak; but if there is no need at all in that speech, and all the more so if there is a concern of a hint of prohibition in it, let the man tremble and be seized, and guard his mouth and his tongue, and be like one mute, not opening his mouth. And they have already said: the fruit of haste is regret (Michlal Yofi 43:27, or a similar wisdom text). And "one who is deliberate is worth four hundred coins" (Berachot 20a[?]). And it is written (Proverbs 24:6): "and there is safety in an abundance of counselors" - included in this is that he take counsel with his own mind and consult with his Maker.
Pele Yoetz 78:5: And all the more so is it proper to make preparation to guard against every evil thing, for at the time of the evil inclination, no one remembers the good inclination - therefore it precedes the wicked. And every day and every hour let him take to heart that he is prone to transgress transgressions that have become like something permitted to him and that people have trampled upon, and let him make preparation within himself, place light within himself, and reckon the punishment and disgrace of every transgression and every evil trait and the reward given for mitzvot, and say thus: why should I transgress against the will of my Maker, my Former, and my Creator, the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He, for the pleasure of a moment? And why should I not have mercy on my own soul, to save it from rebukes for sin, for many are the pains of the wicked? Is it not better for me to separate from the transgression and receive reward for the separation, and fulfill every mitzvah matter with whatever comes to my hand, for I am a Jew? Therefore I hereby accept upon myself with all my strength to be careful and guard with all my strength against this and this and this, and to conduct myself in this way and this way and this way. Such and similar things let him take to heart, or express with his lips, and also in writing, to say, as a remembrance between his eyes - then he shall succeed in his ways and then he shall be wise. And also when he comes to perform a mitzvah, let him not be hasty in his work to do it immediately, as it occurs to him, for there is a way that seems straight to a man, and he thinks to perform a mitzvah, and in the end it turns out to be a transgression, or he comes to regret it and be troubled over his former ways. Therefore a good man shall set his mind on every matter from its beginning, to see through to its end, and conduct his affairs with judgment according to his own capacity, and then let him approach doing it, and may the Almighty be his help.
Pele Yoetz 78:6: And above all, one must make preparation in his mind before performing any mitzvah, and before reciting any blessing, and especially before mentioning the honored Name - for if he does it suddenly, it is disqualified as it comes forth due to lack of intention, being like a body without a soul. And it is known, the saying of the Name, blessed be He, through Isaiah the prophet (29:13): "because this people draws near," and so on, "and their fear of Me is a commandment of men learned by rote - therefore I shall again do a wondrous thing," and so on, may the Merciful One save us. And in the Holy Zohar they said: any commandment performed without dread and love does not fly upward. And they likewise said that any word that comes forth from the mouth without dread and love upon it - of it is written (Numbers 11:33), "the meat was still between their teeth," and "the anger of the LORD burned against the people" - over this let all who grieve, grieve, for we have nearly perished, we have all been lost, God forbid. Therefore the man who fears the LORD and greatly desires His mitzvot shall take to heart, before performing any mitzvah and before every prayer and every blessing, what this mitzvah is and what reason there is in it, and how and in what manner it should be performed, and shall make preparation and arousal within his own soul to perform it with fear, love, and great joy, and as required, in a manner that his mitzvot ascend for favor above, and he not labor in vain nor give birth in haste to the mother of all impurity. This is a great principle for the repair of the body and the soul - go deep into it and dwell long upon it, for everything is within it. Whoever does these things, behold, peace shall never be moved from him. Therefore be strong and courageous to do this, and whoever comes to purify himself is helped from Heaven.
Pele Yoetz 79:1: Trust - Trust is a blessed trait, joy for the body and rest for the soul. And the matter of trust is not that one trust in the LORD that He shall provide all his needs as he wishes and that no evil befall him - for if such were his trust, sometimes his hope would be disappointed, since many righteous men are afflicted and crushed with severe sufferings, and swollen with hunger, and many such evils and troubles that stir to come into the world. Rather, the essence of trust is that one trust in the Name of the LORD that whatever the Merciful One does is for the good, and it is revealed before Heaven that it is good for him and it is done for him - for a person sees with his own eyes, which do not see properly, and calls evil good and good evil, but the LORD knows what is good for him for the service of God, blessed be His Name, and for the repair of the nefesh, ru'ach, and neshamah. Therefore let him be content with whatever comes upon him and accept whatever comes with joy and a good heart, being confident that no evil thing descends from Heaven, only good - and therefore let him cast his burden upon the LORD and lift up his soul to Him, and not labor in vain to do his own will as he wishes, and not press the moment, and not be troubled reckoning many schemes for his own betterment and be distressed over the incidents of the time - for let him believe with complete faith that everything is in the hands of Heaven, and whatever God desires He shall do for his good, and none can save from His hand, and there is no restraint upon the LORD to save whether by much or by little, and He is the One who gives strength to do valiantly, and He performs the will of those who fear Him without their needing to scheme, without their needing to be troubled.
Pele Yoetz 79:2: And those who truly trust in the LORD with a whole heart, not merely with their lips, as many of the common people do, are tested by this: whether they are sincere, in that they do not set aside His will to attain their own will, and He shall be their help and their shield. And for those who do their Maker's will and set aside their own affairs in their trust in God - is it possible that because of this their livelihood would be cut off or their good diminished, heaven forbid? "Shall not the Judge of all the earth do justice?" (Genesis 18:25) - far be it, it should not even be mentioned. On the contrary, whoever trusts in his own sharpness and great effort, or trusts in man, is left in the hand of the one he trusts - and if for a time his fortune helps him, or they repay him some good deed to his face in order to destroy him [i.e., in a way that later ruins him], in the end the wheel turns against him and his wealth is lost, and he descends wondrously, as happens every day - or his wealth is kept for him to his own harm, to trouble him and destroy him. But whoever trusts in the LORD, kindness shall surround him (Psalms 32:10), and if his beginning is of trouble and he lives a life of hardship, heaven forbid to believe it is because he is a servant of God - rather, the LORD is righteous, He tests, and His designs are not miscalculated, and whatever He does is for his good, and honor shall come in the end.
Pele Yoetz 79:3: And the completeness of the trait of trust is that he not trust in man at all and not be exacting toward any person, for let him believe with complete faith that all are agents of the Merciful One, and the Omnipresent has many agents - whether for good or for less good - merit is brought about through the meritorious and guilt through the guilty (Shabbat 34a) - and if the whole world stood on one side of a balance scale to harm or benefit him by even a hair's breadth, and the Omnipresent's decree were on the other side, it would tip the scale against them all. Therefore let him not show favoritism nor flatter nor fear any man, nor labor to grow rich unjustly, for judgment belongs to God, and He gives each man according to his ways, for his own benefit and good. These are some of the ways of the trait of trust, and it has already been treated at length in the holy books, such as Sefer "Chovot HaLevavot" and the holy book "Reshit Chokhmah" and its related works. Happy is the man who studies them diligently, and I have come after them in a brief manner to arouse myself and my own contemporaries. And may the LORD God help me among His people Israel, and may my mouth and my heart be equal, for the sake of the Name, blessed be He, Amen, so may it be His will.
Pele Yoetz 80:1: Acknowledgment - Behold, the matter of acknowledgment that indicates praise, we have already written a portion of it under the entry "Hillul" [praise], with the help of Heaven, and now let us speak of the matter of acknowledgment in the manner of "he confessed and was not ashamed." And there is in this matter a "turning away from evil" aspect - such as acknowledging the falsehood that his fellow speaks and brings him as a witness to. And if he does not wish to lie and utter falsehood with his mouth, but in any case remains silent - silence is like acknowledgment, and this too is a bad trait, for it supports the hands of transgressors and causes evil to his fellow, who relies on his honesty while he shall exchange it and alter it for him.
Pele Yoetz 80:2: But there is a good acknowledgment - such as acknowledging the truth (and this trait is greatly needed, especially for Torah scholars occupied with halachah, who should accept the truth immediately from whoever states it, even the least of the least - let him acknowledge it and not be ashamed to say, even in the presence of many, "the truth is with you, and what I said is an error on my part," and not entrench himself in forced distinctions and excuses to maintain his own words out of love of victory, becoming crooked instead of straight, thereby bringing forth the sword to permit prohibitions and increase division and hatred, so that his Torah is not pleasing, may the Merciful One save us, and it will be sold at a loss - not so one who acknowledges the truth, for even if he is momentarily embarrassed in this world, in the end he shall behold the vision of the Almighty. And according to upright reason, there is no shame here, for every person errs, and we find masters of the Talmud who would say in the presence of many of the congregation of the people of Israel, "what I said in your presence is an error on my part" (Shabbat 63b), and "the acknowledgment of the Rabbis is itself their praise" - there is no better trait than this. And not for nothing did they establish for us to say in prayer every day, "let a person always be God-fearing," and so on, "and acknowledge the truth" - for this matter is entrusted to the heart and requires fear of Heaven, and in any case the words of truth are recognizable, and a person shall be judged by what his own eyes reveal - who is this one who does not acknowledge the truth? It is not fitting to argue matters of halachah with him, and if he resembles an angel of the LORD, then let them seek Torah from his mouth. And in any case, this is the way of perfect men, a holy way - when they see a man who does not acknowledge the truth and twists himself and misrepresents the Torah not according to halachah, they do not entrench themselves in a halachic matter merely to make him acknowledge it, for it is much weariness of the flesh, but rather leave them be - "you shall lodge with your own error" - and if there is a third party, he shall decide between them. Such is the way of Torah scholars whose way is straight.
Pele Yoetz 80:3: And there is another kind of acknowledgment - that one acknowledge what he did wrong even though it brings him to shame, as Judah did, who said (Genesis 38:26), "she is more righteous than I." And of this our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 12b): whoever transgresses a transgression and is ashamed, all his sins are forgiven him. Behold, therefore, the man whose inclination has misled him and who stole or caused some damage to his fellow in secret - when the matter is sought, let him acknowledge it despite the embarrassment, and even if he must pay, for through this he shall be reconciled and correct what he has perverted, and find his own redemption and redeem his soul from going down to the pit. And in such a case, the hour requires strengthening oneself and overcoming one's inclination and revealing his own fault in order to acquire his own world - and it is better that he be shamed before a few people than that he be shamed in the future before thousands and myriads of camps of holy ones. And if he denies it and says he is righteous and saved, he adds transgression to his sin, and moreover causes evil and sin to others, causing suspicion of the innocent and the flame of division to rise higher and higher, and many such things are prepared, and for everything he is destined to give judgment. Let him take all this to heart and overcome his inclination and regret, for "whoever acknowledges and forsakes shall find mercy" (Proverbs 28:13).
Pele Yoetz 81:1: Adornment - Adorning a mitzvah indicates love, for one who serves out of fear seeks only to discharge his obligation, but one who serves out of love, according to the abundance of his affection, is exacting that nothing be lacking in it. And whoever adds to beautify it, this is for him a sign and a wonder that he loves the LORD with all his heart and all his might and increases His honor. And how very much shall the man be ashamed and humbled in the World to Come who is exacting about his clothing and his household utensils and his dwelling place, that they not be torn or soiled and the like, and beautifies his house with plaster and decorations and basins, yet regarding the mitzvot of the LORD is not exacting, using tattered and ugly ones. And happy is the man who loves his Maker and honors the LORD with his wealth and increases expenditures on mitzvot to beautify them - he shall carry a blessing from the LORD of hosts. Correspondingly, in worldly matters, this is not the law - he should not pursue adornment to build fine houses and a pleasant dwelling and to be adorned in embroidered garments and use fine and various vessels, for we are strangers, like travelers on the road and like a guest who turns aside to lodge. And it is true that they said (Eruvin 54a), "if you have, do good for yourself," and everything depends on what kind of person he is - if the LORD has graced him with wealth and abundant possessions, let him clothe himself with what he has and build houses according to his honor - but it is not fitting to waste precious time and labor to grow rich beyond having enough bread to eat and clothing to wear and a place to lodge, in order to attain adornment and increase expenditures on excesses, for all is vanity and vexation of spirit. Therefore, even if the LORD has graced him with wealth and possessions, and then the matter turns and the incidents of the time bring him to live a life of hardship, scant bread and rationed water and a dark house, let him not be exacting and not be distressed, for everything in this world is empty and vain, and we have nothing from life except to serve our Creator and give peace of mind to our Former - let this be our whole aim and all our desire and longing, for there is our home.
Pele Yoetz 82:1: Rising Early - Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 72a[adapted, cf. Berachot 62b]): if one comes to kill you, rise early and kill him first. And the commentators explained that they meant: regarding the evil inclination that comes to kill you, rise early and kill it first - for there is nothing better to kill the evil inclination than rising early at night, at the beginning of the watches, for once he begins to overcome his inclination, rising mighty as a lion to stand for his Creator's service, he shall go on growing, for the LORD stands over him and a thread of kindness is drawn upon him, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explained (Chagigah 12b) on the verse (Psalms 42:9), "by day the LORD commands His kindness, and at night His song is with me." And also, by rising early some hours at the beginning of the watches, he can study with a settled mind and acquire an order of holiness and pour out conversation to seek forgiveness more than in a whole day - and this is the entire fruit of rising early. And woe to those who rise early at the beginning of the watches only to sit in the corners and smoke - the LORD shall say, "they have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, to hew for themselves broken cisterns" (Jeremiah 2:13).
Pele Yoetz 82:2: And it is known that whoever does not serve his Creator at a time when he is free is destined to give an account even for a time when he is not free, for the night was created only for study, and at the time of its own worth there is no song of Torah except at night. And whoever is accustomed to the Holy Zohar shall see with his own eyes the virtue and the great reward of one who studies Torah at night, and especially if he rises at midnight, there is no end to his reward, for he gives great peace of mind to his Maker. And see the book "Reshit Chokhmah" (Gate of Holiness), where a pure man gathered all the matters stated in the words of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, to the point that whoever reads his words shall certainly have his heart kindled and his soul long to rise at midnight. And whoever's portion is among those who sit in the study house can easily rise to fulfill this by sleeping during the day. And the Kabbalists have already written in their books that it is better to sleep even six hours during the day in order to keep this practice of being awake at midnight (and there is already a special remedy to be awake at whatever hour one wishes, and I have appended it to my Beit Tefillati) - and even every other person can train himself to be content with little sleep, and in any case shall strengthen himself like a lion to stand at least in a manner that he himself awakens the dawn.
Pele Yoetz 82:3: And for every good thing, a fence and preparation are needed - care leads to diligence (Avodah Zarah 20b) - so too regarding this matter, the man who fears the LORD and wishes to rise early at the watches and go early to the synagogue to pray with the congregation, and does not wish to lose much good, this is his way, a holy way: he shall not delay in being awake at the beginning of the night even to occupy himself with Torah, and all the more so for an optional matter and frivolous merriment - rather, let him lie down and let his sleep be pleasant, and rise early at the watches, and drink coffee to settle his mind and so that he can properly cleanse his body and relieve himself, and occupy himself with Torah according to the measure the LORD has graced him with, and go early to the synagogue and pray with the congregation. It is found that it is good for him in this world, that his body be healthy and strong, and good for him in the World to Come, that he acquires his own world and prepares delicacies for himself. Not so [the wicked] who linger over wine, pursuing strong drink, whom wine inflames, who do not sleep much of the night, and if they rest a little and rise when the sun comes out over the land, they go out rushed and hurried to their work and their business, having no time to drink coffee nor to relieve themselves, and pray alone a rushed and clipped prayer, and afterward all day they are sick, feeling it in their heads, feeling it in their bowels, their food turned sour and leavened, and strong drink embitters those who drink it - it is found that it is bad for them in this world and bitter for them in the World to Come.
Pele Yoetz 82:4: And it is astonishing about these [foolish] men, who have seen all this with their own eyes many times - that whoever lingers over wine, its beginning is sweet and its end is bitter, even in this world - besides the punishment of the World to Come, which even though they have not seen, they have heard, and all Israel believes it shall certainly be so, and yet they take no instruction (like a dog returning to its vomit, a fool repeating his folly). May the LORD, in His mercy, remove the veil of blindness from our eyes and plant in our hearts love and fear of Him, to do His will. And the commentators have already explained the verse (Proverbs 6:9), "how long, O lazy one, will you lie down to sleep" - and if you say, what does it matter to you, when will you rise from your sleep? So too King David, peace be upon him, said (Psalms 63:7), "if I remember You upon my bed" - "in the watches I meditate on You" - during the time of lying down at the watches, I meditate on You. And this suffices for whoever has a heart to know and eyes to see and ears to hear - let him understand with his heart and hear with his ears, and repent and be healed (Isaiah 6:10).
Pele Yoetz 83:1: Rescue - How much does the mighty man glory in his might (Jeremiah 9:22), and whoever has power and influence and a good name among the officers of the people should glory in this - in rescuing an oppressed person from his oppressor and rescuing the body and money of a Jew from the hand of an idolater. For if the evil of one who hands over a Jew's body or money into the hand of an idolater is so great that it is permitted to kill him even in this age, correspondingly, one who rescues a Jew's body or money increases a good trait and it shall be counted a great mitzvah for him. And all the more so, by an a fortiori argument, if he rescues souls taken to die, for he brings merit to his own soul as though he had fulfilled the entire Torah - for they said (Sanhedrin 37a): whoever sustains one soul of Israel is as though he had sustained an entire world. And of such a case they said (Berachot 27a[adapted]): even the empty ones among Israel are full of mitzvot like a pomegranate - for there are many of the children of Israel who appear on the surface to be empty vessels, but they have in their hand this mitzvah of rescuing Israel, through which they outweigh and surpass the sages and great men of Israel. And it is true that the Holy One, blessed be He, does not take a bribe of mitzvah against transgression and pays them punishment for all the transgressions they do and for every neglected mitzvah they neglect - but He also has abundant reward to give these men who take trouble and labor with all their strength to rescue Israel from the hand of idolaters and to rescue an oppressed person from his oppressor. How good is their portion and how pleasant is their lot! And if the mitzvah of saving a life is so great, all the more so is it doubly good to save one's fellow from sin and bring merit to one's fellow for a mitzvah matter - since they said (Bamidbar Rabbah 21:4; Tanchuma Pinchas 3) that whoever causes another to sin is worse than one who kills him, correspondingly, whoever brings merit to him is greater than one who gives him life.
Pele Yoetz 84:1: Enactment - It is fitting for every community of Israel to make enactments and regulations to set up fences to keep away from prohibition, and not to increase expenses and the like - all according to the need of the hour. And great understanding is needed by those who establish regulations and enactments, that they not make an enactment in a matter that most of the public cannot uphold, lest they come to defy it, breach the fence, and transgress the enactments. Therefore a scale and just balances are needed to conduct their words with judgment, according to the place and the time and according to what kind of people are the residents of the city. And who is wise? He who foresees the consequences (Tamid 32a) - the end of a matter from its beginning.
Pele Yoetz 84:2: And it is good for those who establish regulations to take counsel with the people of the city, and especially with those who seem in their eyes to be quarrelsome and contentious - with them let their words be first, and let them speak to them calmly, words that enter the heart, in a manner that they shall stand at the right hand of their righteousness. And even though it is impossible to first take counsel with all the people of the city, from the smallest to the greatest, and especially with the empty and reckless ones, nevertheless, since they take counsel with the many, there shall be establishment and endurance for their words, for the many shall be their help and shall break the jaws of the wicked - for it is fitting for every person of understanding, even if they did not take counsel with him and made a regulation and enactment that is not proper according to his own opinion, nevertheless, whatever the leaders of the city do according to their own judgment for the sake of Heaven, every good man should go out to greet them in battle for the help of the LORD among the mighty, and strike the heads of the opponents and silence them with rebuke and say to them, be silent. Such is our obligation and such is fitting for us, to accept the regulations and enactments that the leaders of the city establish for us, for the LORD stands over them, and through this there shall be settlement and improvement of the city when they listen to the judge who shall be in those days, to all that he says, even if he says of left that it is right - and woe to a city where each one exalts himself, this one saying one thing and that one saying another, and each one wishes to breach the fence and do what his heart desires, with none to seek and none to inquire - that city shall be destroyed, God forbid (and more is written on this under the entry "Tikkun" [improvement]).
Pele Yoetz 84:3: And how good it would be for those who establish regulations and enactments not to decree by force of excommunication, ban, or the like, lest they find those who breach the fence, and the serpent bite them and cause a great fall, God forbid - but rather let them establish them by force of a communal enactment and a monetary penalty, and it suffices that whoever transgresses the community's enactments has a transgression in his hand. And likewise they should not establish a regulation and forbid something for generations upon generations forever, for they do not know what a day may bring, and perhaps a time shall come when they cannot uphold that regulation and shall gnash their teeth and transgress it - therefore, from the very first hour, they should establish it only for a certain time, or leave room for every judge and leader in his own time to change it, or to add and subtract according to what he sees fit.
Pele Yoetz 84:4: And it is not fitting to dig so much after those who transgress the enactments in secret and in hidden chambers, so that the enactment not be made greater than what the Holy One, blessed be He, Himself commanded us. And it is because of our many sins that transgressors are found, especially in secret, to the point that when Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai blessed his students, he said to them: would that the fear of Heaven be upon you as the fear of flesh and blood (Berachot 28b). Therefore they should not dig too much after them to chastise them, so that they not add to their sin and defiance, and it is their fate that the matter diminish gradually and eventually be upheld. And if they see that it is something many are accustomed to and greatly attached to, they should not uproot the matter entirely all at once, but rather begin by choosing the lesser evil, and slowly, little by little, uproot it entirely, in the manner of what is written (Exodus 23:30), "little by little I shall drive them out." And just as there is a prohibition against favoritism in a matter of judgment, so too regarding enactments and regulations of the community, all faces must be treated equally.
Pele Yoetz 84:5: Equally - one should not favor the poor nor honor the great; one Torah and one law shall be for all of them. Those who do this shall never be moved, provided all their deeds be for the sake of the LORD, the God of the universe.
Pele Yoetz 85:1: Striving - Striving is very necessary for every good thing, whether worldly matters or matters of Heaven - for even though everything is in the hands of Heaven, it has already been stated that sometimes His wisdom, blessed be He, has decreed that according to the striving and diligence one applies, so shall the matter be established. And especially great striving, diligence, and swift action are needed to rescue those taken to die before the wrath of the angel of death's king goes forth, may the Merciful One save us. And how many times have we seen and heard of cases where they could have rescued those taken to die through some small matter, but through laziness, saying "there is no danger, there is no danger," and being reluctant to spend money, in the end the fire grew and the flame rose until they needed to make a great expenditure to rescue them - and would that they could rescue them! Therefore an obligation rests upon all the people within the gates, and especially men who have influence and a good name among the officers, to hasten and rescue whoever falls into their hands - for they are likened to a wild ox in a net: just as a wild ox in a net (that is, a snare), once caught, receives no mercy, so the idolaters show no mercy once one falls into their hands (Bava Kamma 117a). And it is known how great is the mitzvah of saving lives, for which the entire Torah is set aside for the sake of preserving life - all the more so and how much more so must all Israel be obligated to distribute all their money and even sell Torah scrolls for the sake of saving a life. And our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 37a): whoever sustains one soul of Israel is as though he had sustained an entire world - for our first father was one, Abraham, and from him came forth myriads of thousands of Israel, and from the first man the whole world came forth. Therefore an obligation rests, for every good thing, to hasten to strive, and let him do whatever is in his power to do, and the good LORD shall do what is good in His eyes, and He establishes great reward for the one who strives, as though he himself completes and performs it.
Pele Yoetz 86:1: Enjoyment - The sages of ethics have written that this world and the World to Come are troubles to one another, and as long as a person pursues the pleasures and vanities of this world and enjoys this world, it is a sign that he is still outside of attaining the paths of life to merit enjoying the splendor of the Shechinah. And every punishment of the beating of the grave and the like, the judgment of the worm, all of it is because the husk attaches itself to him through his pursuit of the pleasures of this world, which are the portion of the Other Side, and he enjoys them - but the bodies of the righteous, who did not enjoy anything of it at all, are not ruled by it, and of them it is said (Psalms 16:9), "my flesh too shall dwell securely." For they said in the Holy Zohar that whoever is devoted to love of the LORD finds no enjoyment or peace of mind from anything of the pleasures of this world, but delights only in love of the LORD, in the manner of what is written (Song of Songs 7:7), "how fair and how pleasant you are, O love, among delights." But other necessary matters of this world he does as though a demon had compelled him, for the sake of Heaven, in the manner of what Ima Shalom said about Rabbi Elazar, her husband (Bava Metzia 59b).
Pele Yoetz 86:2: And it is fitting for every person to strengthen himself and go deep with pure thoughts to understand and become wise, that all the pleasures of this world are vanity, the work of deception, here one moment and gone the next - and he should not pursue and be drawn after them. And even if he chances upon some enjoyment - such as the scent of money, or his palate tasting good food or good clothing and the like - let him immediately consider that enjoyment as vain and say: if I enjoy this thing, which is vanity and emptiness, so much, all the more so shall the enjoyment of the World to Come be, where the righteous sit and enjoy the splendor of the Shechinah, which is a pleasure beyond fathoming, that we cannot picture even one part in a thousand while our soul is in our body - and more and more, all the more so, should the pleasure of loving God, blessed be He, and fulfilling His mitzvot be, for "better one hour of Torah and good deeds in this world than all the life of the World to Come" (Avot 4:17), and "better one hour of tranquility of spirit in the World to Come than all the life of this world" (ibid.). And through this he should not neglect Torah and mitzvot in order to pursue the pleasures of this world, and if he gave all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned (Song of Songs 8:7). Let such and similar things be considered at every time he finds enjoyment and peace of mind from matters of this world.
Pele Yoetz 86:3: And if he seeks to eat something sweet and pleasant to his palate in order to gain understanding, this shall be counted a mitzvah for him. And such is the custom of men of deeds, to eat or drink something pleasant to their palate at the acceptance of the Sabbath, in order to receive the Sabbath with joy in the manner stated - for from bodily pleasure and joy one can arouse the pleasure of the soul and great joy of the mitzvah, until the bodily pleasure is diminished as vanity and he does not enjoy it [for its own sake].
Pele Yoetz 86:4: And especially regarding the matter of imagined honor, one must strengthen himself very much that if he merits honor, he should not enjoy it at all - for it is written in Sefer Chasidim (8) that whatever a person enjoys of the honor with which he is honored in this world, they deduct from his merits and it diminishes his reward for the World to Come. Behold, therefore, needless to say that it is not fitting to pursue honor, whose evil is great, as we learned (Avot 4:21) that honor removes a person from the world, and in truth it is vanity and vexation of spirit, and whoever pursues it goes from evil to evil, and many evils and troubles shall find him in this world and in the World to Come, and his life is not truly life, as every person of understanding shall see and discern. Rather, even if he flees from honor and honor pursues him - for such is the standard - let him strengthen himself like a lion with pure thoughts not to let his inclination mislead him to enjoy and take peace of mind from honor, but rather, on the contrary, let him be distressed, thinking: my sins shall be smelled by my neighbors - and what shall he do on the day of reckoning if those who honor him see that he is despised and worthless? Shall he not then be sated with disgrace instead of honor? Of such and similar matters the living person shall take to heart, so as not to enjoy this world, and through this he shall behold the vision of the Almighty.
Pele Yoetz 86:5: Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 8a): greater is one who enjoys the fruit of his own labor than one who fears Heaven - for one who enjoys his own labor does not need to flatter anyone, in the manner the commentators explained on the verse (Proverbs 14:24), "the crown of the wise is their wealth (and then), but the folly of fools is folly." And for this reason it is said of one who enjoys his own labor, "and it shall be well with you" (Psalms 128:2), referring to the World to Come - which is not so for one who fears Heaven, for although on the one hand he is happy in this world, even though he awaits his fellow's table, nevertheless he lives a life of peace, quiet, and tranquility - but his good for the World to Come is not complete, as stated.
Pele Yoetz 86:6: And it is stated in the Talmud (Pesachim 113a) that Rav said to Rav Kahana: skin a carcass in the marketplace and earn a wage, and do not say "I am a priest" or "I am a great man." And not as many poor people do - especially if they were once wealthy and their possessions declined - who consider it beneath them to do lowly work, such as being woodcutters and water-drawers and the like, and choose instead to sit in the corners, or wander about the marketplaces and streets, while the members of their household lie in hunger, "the children ask for bread, no one breaks it for them" (Lamentations 4:4), being too ashamed even to ask for and receive charity, and even if they receive it, "a handful does not satisfy" (Berachot 3b). If only they were wise, they would understand that shame is the thief found in the tunnel [i.e. leads to greater loss] - but there is no shame in striving to earn wherever it can be found, and it shall be counted a great mitzvah to enjoy the fruit of one's own labor and bring sustenance to his household, for they said (Ketubot 50a) on the verse (Psalms 106:3), "he who performs righteousness at all times" - this refers to one who feeds his sons and daughters. And if, in any case, he cannot remove the veil of shame from his face, let him go to a place where he is not known and labor, and do whatever is in his power to do to bring sustenance to his household and be satisfied with bread, and it shall be for him an atonement for sin, as we learned (Avot 2:2): fine is Torah study together with proper conduct [an occupation], for the labor of both makes one forget sin.
Pele Yoetz 86:7: Our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Berachot 10a): whoever wishes to enjoy benefit shall enjoy it like Elisha. They were exact to say "like Elisha," for it is written (II Kings 4:8), "and there was a great woman" - she was great in wealth - and also "and she urged him," indicating that one should give with a generous eye. And it is known, the incident of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair, brought in the Talmud (Chullin 7b), who would not wish to enjoy benefit from anyone, saying: there is one who desires but does not have, and there is one who has but does not desire, and in both cases one who enjoys benefit from them commits a trespass - for if he desires it but does not have it, he falls into the category of enjoying a meal that does not suffice its own owner; and if he has it but does not desire it, and gives out of embarrassment, this too has an element of theft, as is known (Sefer Chasidim, 316).
Pele Yoetz 86:8: Behold, therefore, the man who fears the LORD shall fear and be afraid of stumbling into one of these, God forbid - for truly they said (Eruvin 65b): a person is recognized by his pocket. And this is the greatest test for a person: if he overcomes his inclination in the matter of money and his own enjoyment and hates unjust gain in a place where there is a hint of prohibition, this is a sign and a wonder that he is mighty, conquering his own inclination. And whoever fears sin as is proper must be concerned about all prohibitions even in a case of double doubt, and likewise regarding this matter, he shall treat every person as suspect that he might not have it, until he knows for certain that he has it, and that he might not desire it, and be very exacting even over the value of a perutah - and he should not judge by appearances, for such a person may show him a smiling and good-hearted face, for there is one with an evil eye who says to you, "eat and drink," while his heart is not with you. And great is the evil of one who eats the bread of one with an evil eye, to the point that they said in the Holy Zohar that it would be better for a person to strangle himself than to eat the bread of one with an evil eye. Therefore he should not enjoy benefit from another until the matter is as clear to him as the sun, without any doubt, that it is given with a whole heart.
Pele Yoetz 86:9: And whoever goes to collect in the cities - this is the straight path: that he tell his distress to the many and say to them, "my friends, shopkeepers, [give] according to the gift of your hand and according to the blessing the LORD has given you," and be content with whatever they give him the first time, without any refusal at all - then his heart shall be settled and confident that it is given with a whole heart. And it is true that they said (Bava Batra 8b): they compel [people] regarding charity - this applies to one who does not himself need to receive, who can compel with words on behalf of others that they give according to the blessing the LORD has given them, but one who needs to receive, if they give to him out of embarrassment because he compels them with words, it is a transgression and theft in his hand. But what shall those who need to receive and be sustained from others' money do, who cannot be so careful about this - for if they come to be so exacting about it, they might be left lying in hunger? Therefore a person shall strive very much to occupy himself with a trade by which he can be sustained, and if he is a Torah scholar who cannot occupy himself with a trade - and especially in this age, when it is not so possible to make one's Torah study permanent and his occupation occasional, and if it is not befitting the honor of a Torah scholar nowadays - in any case, let him make himself a paid teacher of young children or a synagogue cantor and the like, wherever he can find it, in a manner that he be sustained by the labor of his own hands. And always, whoever wishes to enjoy benefit shall strive very much not to enter into a doubt of theft, and not to cause gossip or any aspect of desecration of the Name, God forbid. And whoever trusts in the LORD, kindness shall surround him, and those who seek the LORD shall not lack any good - for truly they said (Beitzah 16a): a person's sustenance is fixed for him from Rosh Hashanah, except for expenses for a mitzvah, where if he adds, they add to him. And the Omnipresent has many agents and many ways to give each person what is fixed for him, no less and no more. This is a great principle for whoever wishes his entire livelihood to be a good livelihood, with ease and permissibility - let this matter be a remembrance between his eyes, and through this he shall live a life of ease and find favor and good sense in the eyes of God and man. Examine this trait closely and you shall find that it is the elixir of life, for everything is within it. Happy is the man who does this, and the son of man who holds fast to it (Isaiah 56:2) - happy is he in this world, and it is well with him in the World to Come.
Pele Yoetz 87:1: Leadership - Every person must have good leadership, to know how to conduct himself with his young children and his grown children and his wife and his servants, and it is especially necessary for leadership in order to support the community, to know how to conduct oneself with them according to the need of the hour and according to their own understanding and their own character, with great patience. And leadership requires great [skill] to conduct oneself according to need, and especially for the leaders of cities - according to the wisdom of leadership, so shall be the improvement and peace of the city. And even the greatest leader cannot discharge his obligation such that the spirit of the entire city be at ease with him, for not all minds are alike, and even Moses our teacher, peace be upon him, did not fully discharge his obligation with Israel - rather, it is the fate of leaders to discharge their obligation according to the majority. And a fence for this matter is to listen to counsel, for "he who increases counsel increases wisdom" (Avot 2:7), and "there is safety in an abundance of counselors" (Proverbs 11:14). And a second fence is to be deliberate, deliberate, thinking thoughts to foresee the consequences and turning to every side so as not to cause harm. And a third, which surpasses them, is that he take counsel with his Maker and pour out his soul before the LORD - these are matters that have no fixed measure, for not every person and not every occasion are alike. Therefore he must be wise and understanding of his own mind, and if he does not rely on his own knowledge to know how to conduct himself according to the need of the hour, let this general principle be in his hand: to always conduct himself with every person with blessings and a smiling face and sweet words, for this is certainly close to reward and far from loss - and especially in these generations, when insolence increases, even small children do not accept harshness so well, and "a gentle tongue breaks a bone" (Proverbs 25:15) - such vessels [gentle words], and perhaps his words shall be heeded - and through this a person shall be beloved above and cherished below all his days, and the LORD shall not withhold good from those who walk in innocence.
